govdocs-archive_org-nsia-CIALabor_CIA_La: William Greider’s Washington Post piece — Unions Turn to AID After CIA Pullout — covers labor’s break with the agency. The CIA had funded labor fronts. The file belongs to the political archive. The item is a fragment of press history.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-FBIUSRecordingC: This Department of Justice report — on the relationship between... — is a federal file. The declassified report is a primary source. The truncated title suggests a longer work. Researchers value such files. The file belongs to the government archive.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-FordGeraldRPort: This FBI memorandum on the Rankin call — February 24, 1964 — is a Bureau file. The declassified memo is a primary source. J. Lee Rankin was the commission’s counsel. Researchers value such files. The file belongs to the assassination archive.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-FrankelSandor_F: Harold Weisberg’s letter to Sandor Frankel seeking legal counsel — April 14 — is a researcher’s note. Weisberg fought many court battles. Lawyers were his allies. The file belongs to the legal archive. The item is a fragment of correspondence.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-NewOrleansDupli: This essay fragment on the Ruby shooting — creator unknown — is a writer’s piece. Ruby shot Oswald on live TV. The fragment is gripping. The file belongs to the assassination archive. The item is a fragment of the record.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-PearlHarbor_Pea: This item — Pearl Harbor — is a National Security Internet Archive file. The file’s full context is unclear. Its subject seems to be the JFK case. The file may hold a clue. Archivists value such fragments. The item is a fragment of the archive.
the-coverley-papers-from-the-spectator: Joseph Addison's beloved Spectator essays introduce Sir Roger de Coverley, the good-hearted, slightly absurd country squire. Through his visits to London, the theater, and Westminster Abbey, Addison paints a fond, funny portrait of English life in Queen Anne's day. These papers helped invent the modern essay and remain among the most charming in the language.
white-slaves-or-the-oppression-of-the-wo: Minister Louis Albert Banks exposes the grinding poverty of America's working poor in this passionate reform tract. He calls them white slaves — trapped by low wages and harsh conditions — and demands Christian action. A powerful voice from the Social Gospel movement that sought to awaken the nation's conscience.
the-little-warrior: Known in England as Jill the Reckless, Wodehouse's comedy follows Jill Mariner, whose fortune and fiancé vanish together — until new love and a stage career intervene. Bright dialogue and a plucky heroine carry this effervescent romance. Wodehouse at his most charming.
the-radio-amateur-s-hand-book-a-complete: A. Frederick Collins's handbook led the first crop of radio fans into the wireless art — home-built sets, Morse code, and the new wonder of far-heard voices. Plain, full, and keen, it breathes the bright dawn of radio. A prize for all who love old tech and its tale.
modern-broods-or-developments-unlooked-f: Charlotte Yonge's late novel watches modern broods — new generations with unlooked-for developments — with her usual moral interest. The Victorian matron confronts changing times. A fascinating late work from a beloved author. Her shrewd eye notes how the young outgrow the old moral certainties.
the-reverberator: Henry James' Reverberator sends young Americans to Paris, where a gossip column shocks French aristocrats and imperils a romance. His lightest, brightest comedy sparkles with wit. The international theme at play, and James enjoying himself hugely. A delightful short novel.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abbey-of-sain: This entry covers Saint-Victor of Paris, the school of Hugh and Richard. Mystic wisdom flowed from its cloister. Anthony Allaria honors its scholars. Medieval Paris at prayer and study. Adam's sequences were sung in its choir for centuries. Its canons taught half of medieval Paris.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-achard-de-sai: This 1913 reference article on Achard de Saint-Victor — the Victorine abbot and bishop. Vincent Scully honors his learning and holiness. Paris mourned his going to Avranches. A schoolman turned shepherd. His sermons fed the Paris schools. The abbey mourned its wisest son.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-adam-of-st-vi: This 1913 reference piece on Adam of St. Victor — the prince of sequence composers. John Joseph A'Becket celebrates his hymns. His Laudes crucis still rings in choirs. Medieval poetry's brightest singer. The Victorines' glory in verse. His Easter sequence is sung to this day.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-administrator: This 1913 reference piece on the administrator — the prelate who rules a vacant see. Sebastian Messmer explains the office. He keeps the chair warm for the next bishop. Canon law provides for every gap. Order in the Church's transitions. He may not sell the see's lands.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-alexander-bic: A 1913 entry on Alexander Bicknor — the Archbishop of Dublin. Henry Birt follows his troubled primacy. He clashed with kings and popes. Excommunication shadowed his later years. A stormy prelate of medieval Ireland. His register survives in Dublin's archives. His tomb lies in Dublin's cathedral.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-alexis-franco: This 1913 reference piece on Artaud de Montor — the French diplomat and writer on Italy. Georges Goyau sketches his career. His histories praised the papacy. Rome knew him as a friend. A royalist with a Roman heart. His Italy volumes charmed the legitimists.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-aloysius-schl: This 1913 reference piece on Aloysius Schlor — a Jesuit scholar of note. Francis Mershman records his works. The entry preserves his modest fame. The Society honors its learned sons. A teacher in the order's schools. His lectures formed the young Jesuits.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-altar-protect: A 1913 entry on the altar protector — the cover that guards the cloths. Augustin Schulte notes its simple use. Dust and damp fear its shield. Sacristans prize the plain cover. The altar's humble guardian. Its waxed cloth turns the dust. Its hem is weighted with lead.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-antiphonary-o: This 1913 reference piece on the Antiphonary of Bangor — the Irish hymn book. Arthur Ua Clerigh honors its ancient verse. Its hymns are the oldest in Latin. Bangor's monks sang its lines. Ireland's oldest songbook. Its manuscript rests in Milan's library.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-antonis-van-d: This 1913 reference piece on Anthonis Mor — the Dutch master of the portrait. George Williamson praises his courtly likenesses. His Philip II hangs in the Escorial. Spain's grandees sat for his brush. The Netherland's court painter. His workshop trained the Utrecht masters.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-apostolic-exe: A 1913 entry on the apostolic executor — the enforcer of papal rescripts. Andrew Meehan explains his mandate. He carries Rome's will abroad. The curia's arm in distant lands. The executor of the Holy See. His commission bears the papal seal. His powers are strictly defined.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-apparitor: A 1913 entry on the apparitor — the summoner of the ecclesiastical court. Richard Burtsell explains his humble office. He cites the parties to appear. The court's business runs on his feet. The beadle of the tribunal. His staff proclaimed the court's summons.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-arator: This 1913 reference piece on Arator — the Christian poet of the Acts. Paul Lejay praises his Latin verse. His Historia Apostolica sang the apostles. The papal court crowned his poem. The last flower of the Latin muse. His poem was read at St. Peter's.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-asia-minor: This 1913 reference piece on Asia Minor — the cradle of the Eastern Church. Thomas Shahan tells its apostolic glory. The seven churches heard John's letters. Its councils shaped the creeds. The motherland of the councils. Its ruins dot the Turkish hills.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-auditor: This 1913 reference piece on the auditor — the judge of the Roman Rota. William Fanning explains his learned office. He hears the Church's hardest cases. The Rota's decisions guide the tribunals. The canonist's high court. His rochet marks the Rota's rank.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-auxentius-jun: This 1913 reference piece on Auxentius Junior — a bishop of the ancient Church. Thomas Shahan records what is known. The entry preserves his modest fame. The old lists keep his name. A prelate of the early age. His see served the ancient faithful.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-bangor: A 1913 entry on Bangor — the Welsh diocese of the Menai Strait. Edwin Burton gives its ancient story. Its bishops date from the sixth century. The cathedral crowns the university town. A see of the Welsh north. Its bells ring over the strait.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-beelphegor: This 1913 reference piece on Beelphegor — Baal-peor, the Moabite idol. John Francis Fenlon tells his shameful cult. Israel fell to his lure. The plague avenged the apostasy. The idol of the desert's snare. His rites were the pagans' shame. His priests were slain at the command.
